method: Clarified that authorization_event_id is generated by the owner before the frozen spec hash, eliminating a circular dependency; defined backend-neutral meaning in plain language; specified safe recovery when reserve outcome is ambiguous and no capability was returned. Added lesson/design consistency assertions, reran the focused verifier and evidence registry check, rebuilt all 428 pages and the 428-page search index, checked content stats, and visually inspected light/dark full-page screenshots. No provider or external service calls were made. Added an explicit read-only reconcile snapshot type and fake-registry tests for not-found/reserved states; refreshed frozen material and example manifest hashes. Reconciled the state vocabulary so not_found means no authorization record, while authorized means the reservation may be retried; tests now cover not-found, authorized, and reserved event chains. Added an external recovery-operator contract for stranded reservations: recover_abort requires registry-verified evidence from the trusted isolated runtime that the candidate never started; otherwise the run remains reserved for investigation. Added protocol and fake-shape tests. Tightened recovery evidence input to require both an artifact reference in the trusted runtime-audit namespace and its SHA-256; external registry must fetch and verify the artifact rather than trust operator-supplied digest. Expanded reconcile snapshots to carry the sanitized event payload alongside its digest so callers can inspect the authorization/reservation/terminal chain; the contract explicitly excludes holdout inputs, labels, raw candidate output, credentials and capabilities. Made the reserve adapter return the sanitized authorization/reservation event snapshot and added a pre-execution validation gate for actor roles, frozen run identities, event linkage, UTC order, allowlisted payload shape, and canonical event hashes. Clarified that the current max_output_bytes check runs after candidate.execute materializes a response and therefore cannot prevent adapter-side buffering; the formal adapter must bound bytes while reading IPC/stream and terminate the candidate at max_output_bytes + 1. Added regression assertions in the W6 verifier. Updated docs/PROGRESS.md, the Stage 5 plan, course lesson, and evaluation README to distinguish post-return structural output validation from required streaming/IPC byte enforcement in the formal isolated runtime. W6 verifies the lesson wording. Promoted the official holdout result contract to schema v3: the runner computes report_sha256 over the canonical result body before terminal append, the terminal registry event must store the same digest, and acceptance recomputes the body hash while excluding registry/evidence envelope fields to avoid self-reference. Added mutation and event-mismatch regression tests. Completed final project validation and refreshed evidence after the v3 result-hash change. Closed a further plan/code gap: the acceptance gate previously checked array order and unique event IDs but ignored previous_event_id pointers. It now requires authorized -> reserved -> terminal linkage; added a regression test that breaks the terminal pointer while preserving event order and all IDs. Final project validation and light/dark visual review completed after adding previous_event_id chain validation.

observations.trace: Focused W6 verifier 4/4; capstone acceptance suite 52/52; P5 evaluation suite 51/51 (official runner contracts 33/33); verify:examples passed; evidence registry 14/14; pnpm test 115/115; typecheck and lint passed; production build and search index passed (428 pages; 15,602 words); depth-check 0 hard errors / 2 advisories; verify:depth passed; content stats 144/144. Light/dark screenshots show article width 792px at 1300px viewport with no horizontal overflow; both viewport captures are 1300x1000. Existing favicon 404 is the only browser console error. No provider or external service calls. Added a plain-language, one-time gate-key contract: capability is short-lived, bound to the frozen run/candidate/dataset/runtime, never exposed to candidate/logs/reconcile, and not reissued after an ambiguous reservation; W6 verifier asserts the contract is present in plan and lesson. This is a design requirement only; no external capability service was exercised. Rebuilt the production site (428 static pages) and Pagefind index (428 pages / 15,602 words), ran depth-check (0 hard errors, 2 advisories), verify:depth, content stats 144/144, capstone acceptance tests 52/52, W6 verifier 4/4, and git diff --check. Full-page light/dark captures are 1300x7870; the page is visually legible with no horizontal overflow at 1300px; existing favicon 404 remains the only browser console error. Added a service-level registry conformance matrix for concurrent reservation, lost response/capability handling, capability scope and replay, executor-vs-recovery terminal races, idempotency and commit ambiguity, restart durability, and redaction. The W6 verifier asserts that both the plan and lesson include these checks. The matrix specifies evidence required from an actual registry; no external service has yet been tested. Rebuilt the 428-page production site and visually inspected full-page light/dark lesson captures at a 1300px viewport (1300x8002; no horizontal overflow). The only browser console error is the pre-existing favicon 404. Added a fillable official holdout run record template with named roles, frozen component hashes, exact decimal-string budgets, quality thresholds, stop conditions, preflight checks, signatures, evidence paths, and post-run classification. The form defaults to no-go and leaves real owner/budget/service identities blank; it does not authorize a run. W6 verifier checks the template and the plan links to it. Tightened the run record to require conflict-of-interest separation: owner/executor/recovery are distinct; scorer is separate from candidate implementation/execution/runtime operation; reviewer is separate from implementation/execution/scoring. Split registry terminal state (consumed/aborted/failed/not-yet-terminal) from observation certainty (known/unknown), and required completed records to stay in a controlled evidence store. W6 verifier asserts these fields and the plan gates. Clarified run-record registry snapshots: not_found means no authorization event; authorized means authorization exists but no reservation and expiry/spec/run identity must still be checked; reserved and terminal states are irreversible; unavailable is not evidence of not_found. W6 verifier asserts the status vocabulary and non-equivalence. Expanded service-level conformance with concurrent authorization of the same holdout/run under conflicting frozen specs (only one may win) and an explicit scorer label-release gate: deny label access while runtime is open or output unsealed; release only to the authorized scorer after closure and output hash sealing. Updated preflight and W6 assertions. These remain requirements for a real service; no external registry was exercised. Added two security-critical registry service tests: concurrent owner authorization with conflicting frozen specs must have a single winner for a holdout/run, and the scorer must be denied hidden labels until the candidate runtime closes and the output hash is sealed. Updated run-record preflight and W6 assertions. The matrix remains a required future external-service test; it was not run against a real registry. Aligned the independent handoff JSON template with the formal run record: schema v2 replaces ambiguous name_or_id fields with stable subject IDs, records owner/executor/custodian/runtime/scorer/recovery/reviewer/release roles, and separates registry state, execution observation, and quality decision with explicit initial values. HANDOFF.md now links to the holdout preflight and keeps completed records in controlled evidence storage. W6 asserts these shape and privacy boundaries. Final validation after handoff-template alignment: pnpm verify:examples passed, including evaluation 51/51 (official runner contracts 33/33), live-runner 25/25, drill-report 16/16, release-candidate 10/10, and 13 release-candidate subtests; pnpm verify:evidence 14/14; W6 verifier 4/4; JSON parsing and git diff --check passed. These checks validate local materials and hashes only, not a real registry or holdout. Clarified the JSON record distinguishes the holdout reviewer from the general handoff reviewer rather than duplicating an ambiguous reviewer_subject_id field; W6 verifier asserts both fields. Removed the duplicate holdout consumed boolean from handoff JSON v2. registry_state is the consumption authority, while runner_outcome, execution_observation, and quality_decision independently record runner report, certainty, and scored result. W6 asserts the split and the guide explains it; full verifier passes. Upgraded the independent handoff record to schema v3 with assurance profile, risk-owner and trust-domain fields, explicit threat-model scope, and witness fingerprint/terminal receipt requirements; added schema and CLI cross-domain checks and extended the W6 verifier. Reconciled the W6 assertion with the implemented official runner schema v3 (the evidence envelope remains v6). Current verification: handoff/evidence-registry tests 21/21, W6 4/4, handoff template validation, verify:examples, test:links 7/7, and git diff --check pass. No production registry, independent witness, or official blind run was exercised.

limitations: The owner-preallocated authorization event ID and recovery rules are a documented local contract; no trusted external registry or custodian was connected.
No isolated candidate runtime, independent scorer, official blind run, or independent human review was performed.
The prior bounded live smoke remains incomplete and does not establish a successful notification or sink non-receipt.
Reconciliation is represented as a local protocol/data shape only; it does not implement or authenticate an external registry.
The fake reconciliation tests cover state-shape contracts only; concurrency linearization and authorization remain properties for an external service to prove.
The fake recover_abort test validates local request shape only; it cannot authenticate runtime evidence or prove that a candidate did not execute.
The local fake checks the evidence reference namespace and digest shape only; an external registry must authenticate the audit source and verify artifact bytes.
The fake snapshot includes fixture event fields only; external response filtering and payload-hash correctness require independent service-level verification.

Snapshot validation detects structural inconsistency only; a malicious or compromised registry can still fabricate internally consistent events, so external authentication and append-only controls need independent evidence.
